posts: "How does Swop make money?" is a fair question and most crypto apps answer it badly — usually by not answering it. Here's the whole thing, including the parts where the answer is "we don't" 🧵
1/ The published number is one: SwopPay checkout charges 0.5%. A seller lists something, a buyer pays, Swop keeps 0.5%. Not a subscription, not a cut of your balance, not a fee for using the wallet.
2/ And it's the same on both rails — 0.5% whether the buyer pays by card or in crypto. One number, not a headline rate with a quieter one behind it.

3/ Why a transaction fee and not a spread? Swop is self-custodial — keys are generated and held on your device. A platform that never holds your funds has no balance to earn float on. That business model simply isn't available to us.
4/ And gas: Swop covers the network fee. It's a cost absorbed, not a charge passed through to you and not a margin quietly taken on top.

5/ Referrals, stated precisely: a referrer earns half of the swap fees generated by people they refer, for 12 months after signup. A share of what Swop collects — not a surcharge. A referred user pays exactly what an unreferred one pays.
6/ Most referral programmes are funded by charging somebody more. This one comes out of Swop's own share. Rewards are paid in SWOP: the fees collected buy SWOP, which is credited to the referrer.

7/ The AI agent runs on credits denominated in the SWOP utility token. That's a pricing mechanism, not an investment claim — the agent is a metered product and SWOP is the unit it's metered in. We're not dressing that up.

8/ And the part most companies would leave vague: Swop charges no fee on perpetual futures or prediction markets today. Not an undisclosed rate — no rate. It's being looked at, so read it as true of today.
9/ That's the whole business model. One published fee, a referral share funded out of it, agent credits, and two surfaces with nothing charged yet. https://www.swopme.co/blog/how-does-swop-make-money
